_comment: Ratchet baseline for `npm run check:src-complexity-drift`, RE-CAPTURED 2026-08-20 at HEAD f631c578, after the repo-wide complexity campaign took src/ from 179 violations to 5. Measured by that script's own findViolations() -- ESLint `complexity` + `sonarjs/cognitive-complexity` hard-overridden to error/9, scoped to the SCOPES list in that file (src/server, src/assistant, src/features, src/widgets, src/seo, src/platform/export, src/analytics, src/media, apps/site-chat/src), excluding __tests__ and __measurements__. Do NOT compare these counts to any other complexity number in this repo without checking both use the same tool, threshold and scope. The previous baseline held 105 entries covering src/server/routes ONLY; 103 of those were fixed rather than grandfathered.
_comment_2026-09-03: Added apps/website/src/features/external-mcp/save-form.ts's mergeExternalMcpSavePrefill entry below as an intentional exception, not a fix-later debt item. The function is one early return plus ~15 independent `input.x ?? existing.x [?? undefined]` fallback lines -- zero nesting, no shared control flow between fields. Verified directly: with this function reverted to that exact inline form and every OTHER function in the same file left refactored, a fresh `eslint --rule complexity:9,sonarjs/cognitive-complexity:9` scan reports only the cyclomatic-18 line below and NO cognitive-complexity violation at all for this file -- the file's earlier cognitive-36 report was entirely attributable to buildExternalMcpSaveFormFields (fixed, not exempted; see the commit history on save-form.ts). Splitting this function would mean inventing artificial groupings across ~15 unrelated scalar fields, which is strictly worse than the flat form. Reviewed and directed by the coordinator (non-authoring reviewer) on 2026-09-03; owner: whoever next materially changes this function's field list -- re-count `??` chains against the 9 ceiling at that time rather than assuming the exemption still fits.
_comment_2026-09-03_ratchet: RE-CAPTURED 2026-09-03 at HEAD 8f1da001 by running THIS script's own findViolations() directly (see capture provenance rule in check-src-complexity-drift.ts's header) -- not typed from the `ADS-memory/reports/COMPLEXITY-DEBT-REMAINING-2026-09-03.md` audit prose, which was already one commit stale by the time this ran (that report counted 70 across 41 files; live capture found 80 across 46 files -- 9 net-new from other agents concurrently editing this shared tree during the same session, most visibly apps/website/src/assistant/external-mcp-oauth.ts's cognitive-complexity jumping to 32). This is a full REPLACEMENT of the violations array, not an append: the prior baseline's 5 `src/...`-path entries (features/settings/migration.ts, features/theme/validation/references.ts, features/vendor-credentials/dual-read.ts, server/inbound/admin-http/routes/plugins/uninstall.ts x2) were dead references left over from the 2026-09-02 apps/website repoint (see check-src-complexity-drift.ts SCOPE HISTORY) -- NOT fixed, just unreachable at their old path -- and are folded back in below at their live `apps/website/src/...` path rather than double-counted. Decision (fix-worst vs. baseline-and-ratchet, delegated to this pass): baseline-and-ratchet, reusing this exact existing mechanism rather than inventing a second one. Reasoning: (1) this gate is a proven, CI-BLOCKING ratchet today -- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `gate-src-complexity` step feeds the `Gate summary (build-and-test)` aggregator that `exit 1`s the job on any FAIL outcome, so freezing the current 80 here genuinely stops backsliding, it is not a report-only checkbox; (2) 80 violations across 46 files is not reviewable as a single mechanical refactor pass without materially raising regression risk in security/credential-adjacent code (execution-credential-store.ts, external-mcp-oauth.ts, site-credential-store.ts, webhooks/seal-aad-invariant.ts, webhooks/secret-scan-guard.ts, custom-credentials/store.ts) -- exactly the kind of change the standing no-silent-behavior-change rule warns against attempting at volume; (3) most scores are modestly over threshold (10-13 of 9), not pervasively unreadable, so the marginal readability gain from an unreviewed mechanical batch is small relative to the risk; (4) `external-mcp-oauth.ts`'s cognitive-32 is the one outlier worth flagging back to whoever owns that file next, rather than silently grandfathering it as routine debt. Nothing in this file was fixed in this pass -- see the handoff report for the full file list and per-file scores.
